h1: The 5 Best Midea Dehumidifiers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 Midea dehumidifiers scored on pint capacity, drainage options, noise and Wi-Fi control, from the Cube 20 to 50 pint models.
summary: The Midea 50 Pint dehumidifier for basements is the best Midea for most damp homes: a 4,500 sq ft coverage claim, 49 dBA on low and Wi-Fi control. The Midea Cube 50 adds a built-in pump for draining uphill. The Cube 35 and Cube 20 fit smaller spaces, and the 22 Pint is the quiet, Energy Star choice for a 1,500 sq ft basement.
intro: Most dehumidifier mistakes happen at the drain, not the compressor. A unit that fills a bucket in half a day is useless in a basement you visit once a week, so the real question is where the water goes. Midea builds its lineup around that question, from a Cube with a larger tank and drain hose to models with a pump that can push water up and out.

So we ranked the five current Midea models by drainage freedom first, then capacity, noise and control. We reviewed the Cube 20, 35 and 50 pint units plus two classic Midea models, using their listings. Where a coverage figure is truncated in the listing we state only what is shown, and we treat capacity figures as the manufacturer's claim, not a measurement.

products.name: Midea 50 Pint Dehumidifier for Basement
products.verdict: A 50 pint basement model with a 4,500 sq ft claim, 49 dBA low mode and Wi-Fi control.
products.description:
This 50 pint Midea targets large damp spaces, with a 4,500 square foot coverage claim, 49 dBA quiet operation on low mode and Wi-Fi control from your phone. Remote control matters in a basement because you can watch humidity without going downstairs.

It ranks first because it combines the largest capacity class with the clearest noise figure and app control. Against the Cube 50 it lacks the built-in pump, so it needs a gravity drain or a bucket, but it costs the same $200 to $500. It is a better fit for a big, open lower level.

Buy it if the whole basement is damp. The caveat: 49 dBA is quiet for its size but audible in a finished room, and drainage is up to you.
products.idealFor: Large basements that stay damp year-round.
products.skipIf: You need to drain uphill without a pump.

products.name: Midea Cube 50 Pint Dehumidifier
products.verdict: A built-in water pump drains vertically or horizontally, with a tank 3x larger and Wi-Fi control.
products.description:
The Cube 50 pairs a tank described as three times larger with a built-in water pump that drains vertically or horizontally, plus Wi-Fi control. The pump is the standout: it lifts water to a sink or window instead of needing a floor drain.

It ranks second because the Midea 50 Pint lists a 4,500 sq ft claim and a stated noise figure, which this listing omits. Both sit in the same $200 to $500 tier. The Cube wins where a basement has no floor drain and the nearest outlet for water is above the unit.

Choose it if the floor drain is across the room or absent. The caveat: pumps add a moving part, so check the hose length and keep the intake clear.
products.idealFor: Basements without a floor drain nearby.

products.name: Midea Cube 35 Pint Dehumidifier for Basement
products.verdict: A 35 pint Cube with a drain hose, a tank up to 3x larger and a no-bucket option.
products.description:
The Cube 35 collects up to 35 pints with a drain hose, a tank described as up to three times larger and a no-bucket option for removing moisture continuously. It sits between the 20 and 50 pint models.

It ranks third because the 50 pint units cover more space, and the Cube 35 sits in the same $200 to $500 tier as them. The reason to pick it is size: a 35 pint unit suits a mid-size basement without paying for the largest class.

Buy it if your damp area is mid-sized and you want hose drainage. The caveat: the listing gives no noise, Wi-Fi or coverage numbers, so confirm those before buying.
products.idealFor: Mid-size basements that need hose drainage.
products.skipIf: You want app control or a big-space unit.

products.name: Midea 22 Pint Dehumidifier for Basement
products.verdict: A 22 pint unit for 1,500 sq ft spaces, 47 dBA and Energy Star certified with 31 percent energy savings.
products.description:
Midea's 22 pint model targets 1,500 square feet, runs at 47 dBA and is Energy Star certified, with a claimed 31 percent energy saving. It is the quietest figure in the ranking.

It ranks fourth because 22 pints is a small capacity and the listing offers no drain hose or pump detail. It costs $100 to $200, so it beats the bigger Cubes on price and electricity use. For a small basement or a crawlspace entry it is enough.

Choose it for a smaller damp area where noise and running cost matter. The caveat: the 31 percent figure is a manufacturer claim, and a 22 pint unit is undersized for a big or very wet basement.
products.idealFor: Small damp areas where noise and power use matter.
products.skipIf: Your basement is large or very wet.

products.name: Midea Cube 20 Pint Dehumidifier for Basement
products.verdict: A 20 pint Cube with a drain hose and a tank up to 3x larger, for $100 to $200.
products.description:
The Cube 20 collects 20 pints with a drain hose, a tank described as up to three times larger and a no-bucket option. It is the smallest Cube and the cheapest entry to the line.

It ranks last because 20 pints limits it to small spaces, and the Midea 22 Pint adds a quoted 1,500 sq ft claim, a noise figure and Energy Star status for the same $100 to $200. The Cube's draw is the hose-and-large-tank design, which saves emptying.

Buy it for a small room, closet or laundry nook. The caveat: with no noise, coverage or Wi-Fi details listed, it is a basic option.
products.idealFor: Small rooms, closets and laundry areas.

whatMatters.detail: Pint capacity is how much moisture a unit removes per day under test conditions. Bigger numbers suit larger or wetter spaces, but oversized units run less efficiently in small rooms. Midea ranges from 20 to 50 pints here. Match capacity to square footage and dampness, and treat the listed number as a manufacturer claim.

A built-in pump pushes water through a hose up to a sink, window or drain above the unit. Without one, you rely on gravity or a bucket. The Midea Cube 50 lists a pump that drains vertically or horizontally. Check the listing for pump height limits and hose length before relying on it.

A drain hose lets the unit empty itself into a floor drain or sink continuously, so you never empty a bucket. The Cube line lists this. It requires a drain lower than the unit. Look for the words drain hose or continuous drainage, and measure the distance to your drain.

Dehumidifiers run all day, so noise matters if the unit shares space with living areas. Stated figures like 47 dBA and 49 dBA on low are quiet for the category. Many listings omit the number. Prefer a stated figure, and remember that low fan speed removes less moisture.

Wi-Fi control lets you set humidity targets and check status from a phone. In a basement you rarely visit, that removes guesswork about whether the tank is full or the unit is running. The Midea 50 Pint and Cube 50 list it. Confirm app support for your phone before counting on it.

faq.q: What size Midea dehumidifier do I need?
faq.a: Match pints to space and dampness. The Midea 22 Pint is aimed at 1,500 sq ft, while the Midea 50 Pint lists 4,500 sq ft. Choose the next size up if the area is very wet or poorly ventilated.

faq.q: What is the most common dehumidifier mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring drainage. A full tank shuts the unit off, so humidity returns. The Cube models with a drain hose, or the Cube 50 with a pump, avoid emptying buckets in basements you rarely visit.

faq.q: Is the Cube 50 worth it over the Midea 50 Pint?
faq.a: If you have no drain nearby, yes. The Cube 50's built-in pump moves water up and out, while the Midea 50 Pint lists a clearer 4,500 sq ft claim and a stated noise level at the same $200 to $500 tier.

faq.q: How do I set up a drain hose?
faq.a: Attach the hose to the drain outlet, run it downhill without kinks to a floor drain or sink, and secure the end. On a Cube 20 or 35, leave the bucket out. Test by running it and watching for leaks.

faq.q: How do I maintain a dehumidifier?
faq.a: Clean the filter every few weeks, wipe the tank and keep the intake clear. On pump models like the Cube 50, flush the line occasionally. Keep the unit away from walls so air flows freely.

faq.q: What humidity level should I set?
faq.a: Many aim for roughly 45 to 50 percent in a basement. Lower settings run the compressor longer and cost more. With Wi-Fi models, check the readings over a week before adjusting the target.

finalTake: The Midea 50 Pint is the best Midea dehumidifier for most basements, with a big capacity claim, a stated 49 dBA low mode and app control. Choose the Cube 50 when there is no floor drain, and the 22 Pint for a small, quiet space. Whatever you buy, sort out the drain first.
